documents.title: Design and write AI policies
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on AI itself. It tells each instructor to decide AI use per course from learning goals: "each instructor will need to do this work for each course they teach", so the stance is delegates.
documents.summary: CATLOE guide that walks instructors through deciding and communicating a course AI policy in three phases: identify the role of AI in learning, draft the policy with reasons, and open a conversation with students. It is advisory and never sets a university rule.

documents.title: Addressing Dishonesty and AI
documents.stance_why: The page is advice to instructors, not a rule: it offers "eight" practices to "minimize student cheating" and sets no AI permission or ban, so it leaves the decisions to instructors (delegates).
documents.summary: CATLOE guidance on reducing dishonesty in student writing including AI use. It argues for prevention through low-stakes assessments, communicated value, and course-specific assignments rather than detection.
